summary: Frontend verification of the four new features (Recorder, Cue Points, Energy Sort, One-Tap Mix) at 1920x1080. Seeded license via addInitScript, granted mic permission, created TEST playlist, uploaded /tmp/{a220,b330,c440}.wav, clicked track-list-panel to unlock AudioContext. Recorder start→stop→download works and yields 'Hot Live 95 Session ...webm'. Cue Points had a critical runtime error 'formatTime is not defined' that broke chip stacking and subsequent clear/arm flow — I fixed the missing import in App.js. After the fix, cue-point-0 + cue-point-1 stack, cue-points-clear removes them, and arming the cued track to standby (standby-track-name populates) works with zero pageerrors. Energy Sort reorders and shows banner '✨ Playlist re-sorted for smooth tempo & harmonic flow' (in this seeded fixture BPMs were already ascending 120/129/140, so visual row order didn't change — algorithm ran without crash). One-Tap Mix: 'M' hotkey correctly armed next track to standby (standby-track-name='a220' after M on track 0); pressing M/1-TAP with empty state does not crash. Regression: crossfader-rail, standby-sync, fader-curve-smooth, auto-cue-next-toggle, deck-waveforms all present; /live page loads and shows NOW PLAYING.

integration_issues.issue: After M hotkey arms standby and (per spec) auto-TAKEs on next beat, the second 1-TAP button click found standby empty in the same session — could not deterministically re-verify the auto-take timing window. Music was 'OFF AIR' during the second attempt (short 8s samples likely ended), so the arm path had no on-air track. Recommend main agent verify the auto-TAKE scheduling with a longer sample or by re-playing before the 2nd tap.

issues: Pre-existing hydration warning: <span> injected inside <option> by x-source instrumentation. Not caused by these features.

action_items: Verify my fix in /app/frontend/src/App.js (added `import { formatTime } from '@/lib/format';`). Root cause: line 1492 used formatTime() in setBanner without importing it — every click on data-testid='cue-set-point' threw a synchronous runtime error which broke React state consistency for cue points (second chip wouldn't render, cue-points-clear appeared to not run).
Consider verifying One-Tap auto-TAKE beat scheduling with a track longer than 8s so the entire arm→sync→take path can be observed twice in a row.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG (fixed by me): App.js line 1492 called `formatTime(t)` without importing it from '@/lib/format'. This is a runtime ReferenceError inside the setCuePoint handler. Root cause: missing import statement at top of App.js. Since setBanner's template literal is evaluated synchronously in the click handler, the throw prevented reliable follow-up UI updates and could have blocked adjacent state commits. Fix applied: added `import { formatTime } from '@/lib/format';`.

energySort() greedily picks nearest bpmCost + harmonic penalty; correct O(n^2). Note that if input is already sorted by BPM and harmonic-compatible (as with the seeded tonal WAVs — all camelot 8A/9A/8A), the resulting order is identical to input. Consider a subtle banner tweak like 'Already flowing' when no reorder occurred, so users get positive feedback.

toggleRecord catches only startRecording failures; stopRecording rejection isn't handled — but engine implementation makes this unlikely. anchor download uses createObjectURL/revokeObjectURL correctly (6s timeout).
setCuePoint dedupes and caps at 4 hot cues; sorted ascending. Good idempotency.
oneTapMix delegates to engine which does arm+sync+scheduled take; App-side listener only binds 'KeyM' and prevents default — clean.

rca of the issue: Runtime ReferenceError 'formatTime is not defined' at App.js:1492. Reproduction: click data-testid='cue-set-point' after loading a track in the CUE panel. Root cause: missing named import from '@/lib/format' in App.js. Mitigation: added the import statement; verified 0 pageerrors on re-run and both hot-cue chips stack, clear works, and arming a cued track loads standby-track-name correctly.
